content: Skatole, also known as 3-methylindole, is a mildly toxic organic compound that appears as a white crystalline solid. It belongs to the indole family of compounds. Skatole is naturally present in feces, where it is produced from the amino acid tryptophan in the mammalian digestive tract. It is also found in beets and coal tar. The compound is characterized by a strong fecal odor, but at low concentrations, it exhibits a floral scent. This floral aroma is present in several flowers and essential oils, including those of orange blossoms, jasmine, and Ziziphus mauritiana. Skatole is widely used in the fragrance industry as both a scent and a fixative in perfumes. It also serves as an aroma compound. The name skatole is derived from the Greek root skato-, meaning dung. In toxicological studies, skatole has been shown to induce pulmonary edema in goats, sheep, rats, and certain strains of mice. It appears to selectively target Clara cells in the lungs, which are the primary site of cytochrome P450 enzymes. These enzymes metabolize skatole into a reactive intermediate known as 3-methyleneindolenine. This intermediate damages cells by forming protein adducts. Skatole can be found as a white crystalline or fine powder solid, which tends to brown with aging. It is a nitrogen-containing compound, and one of its rings is a pyrrole. The compound is soluble in alcohol and benzene. When treated with potassium ferrocyanide (K4Fe(CN)6·3H2O) and sulfuric acid (H2SO4), it produces a violet color. Structurally, skatole has a double-ring system that exhibits aromaticity. The system is continuous, planar, and adheres to the 4n + 2 rule, as it contains 10 π electrons. Skatole can be synthesized through the Fischer indole synthesis, a method developed by Emil Fischer. It is one of several compounds that attract male orchid bees, which collect the chemical to synthesize pheromones. This property makes skatole a common bait for attracting and studying these bees. In a 1994 report by five major cigarette companies, skatole was listed as one of the 599 additives used in cigarettes. In this context, it functions as a flavoring ingredient.
